objective: Provide provider-neutral bounded context admission for long-horizon agents with trust filtering, token-aware deterministic selection, compaction lineage, generation fencing, replay/tamper protection, and explicit non-authority semantics.

research_inputs.finding: Current context-engineering guidance treats context as a finite attention budget and recommends just-in-time retrieval, progressive disclosure, compaction, structured note-taking, and high-signal context curation.
research_inputs.implementation_impact: FAISAL adds deterministic bounded selection and records omitted context plus optional exact-source compaction evidence without performing model summarization.

research_inputs.finding: Current long-running-agent guidance recommends incremental progress, persistent progress artifacts, clean checkpoints, and explicit testing to prevent one-shot work and premature completion.
research_inputs.implementation_impact: Context plans are generation-bound, replay-protected, and auditable as control-plane artifacts for long-horizon continuation.

research_inputs.finding: The current MCP specification defines opt-in asynchronous Tasks and emphasizes consent, privacy, tool safety, and treating tool descriptions/annotations as untrusted unless trusted by policy.
research_inputs.implementation_impact: Context evidence and compaction receipts remain data-only and cannot authorize tool invocation or side effects.

research_inputs.finding: Current persistence guidance separates thread-scoped checkpoints from cross-thread stores, warns that in-memory persistence is lost on restart, and recommends retention/pruning for unbounded checkpoint growth.
research_inputs.implementation_impact: FAISAL context admission bounds items/tokens and binds selected and omitted digests to generation and observed time.

features: trust, quarantine, generation, and expiry filtering

limitations: The contract selects references and verifies digests; it does not retrieve data, summarize context, call models, execute tools, or enforce distributed quotas.
Token estimates, trust ranks, source digests, and compaction receipts are caller-supplied evidence and are not independently attested by this local module.
A compaction receipt proves only exact source-digest coverage and bounded summary metadata; it does not prove semantic faithfulness of the summary.
The benchmark measures local Python receipt overhead and excludes model, network, storage, browser, accelerator, and kernel latency.
The real held-out evaluation uses deterministic fixture adapters and does not measure context quality, frontier models, general intelligence, browser autonomy, or robotics capability.
No physical accelerator, TPM, secure enclave, production KMS, independent builder, live multihost deployment, or external security review was exercised.
This evidence does not claim AGI capability, production approval, superiority to Linux, or closure of existing external release blockers.
